questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My grandmother was French, a student of Sorbonne and lived in Paris. Thus, I had the opportunity to come and visit her in Paris throughout my childhood every summer. However, after her death in 2012 I felt as if I had lost the strong connection, I had to my grandmother's city which is why I was so thrilled to have the opportunity to go back and study at the very same faculty that my grandmother studied English at many years ago. Besides I was very motivated to improve my French, and I knew my grandmother wanted me to be able to speak it well. Therefore, an Erasmus exchange at Sorbonne was the perfect choice for me.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you do the régistration administrative" (general registration) "registration pédagogique" (inscription to the specific courses). The first is done at a meeting which you are invited to attend through email. The latter is a most difficult process where you have to write to all the specific professors and ask to then if they will inscribe you to their classes. It is very difficult to get an overview of the different classes as they are in many different folders and documents.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Very little thorugh email or phone. It is not possible to get in touch with the administration between july and september because they will be on vacation.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not successful. I had hoped I could have taken classes at Panthéon Sorbonne since I am a student of political science in Denmark however for some reason I was inscribed to Faculté des Lettres which is more humanistic. I tried to contact Sorbonne to see if I could take classes at Panthéon even though I was inscribed to a different faculty, but I could not get through before it was too late because the administration was on vacation.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find other students from KU and work together. It will be difficult so be prepared for that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The teaching was on a very high level with. All the teachers were professors or expert which is more than could be said about the classes at KU.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: they vere on a very high level though they often lacked any visual presentation or itneractivity

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The dissemination was certainly much poorer at Sorbonne than at KU however the classes were on a much higher level as I spent considerably more time with professors at Sorbonne than at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Philosophie de la Politique. Programmation du Python. Linguistique et phonétique Française. Sociologie des inégalités. Sociologie des migrations. Sociologie du droit. Sociologie du science et environnement.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would like to recommend the very exiting course: Sociologie des inégalites. The teacher used PowerPoint. Also I would like to recommend philosophie de la politque. The classes were on a very high level though the dissemination were poor. The lectures by the famous professor Tavoillot where excellent and they had visual presentations.
